abstract:
The Environmental Foundations of Polycrisis Resilience is a foundational publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).
It advances an integrated environmental approach connecting climate adaptation, pollution reduction, clean energy transitions, environmental infrastructure, and sustainable development— positioning environmental improvement as a core mechanism for strengthening the long-term capacity of populations and societies to withstand interconnected global risks.

keyFindings.title: Environmental conditions are fundamental determinants of human and systemic vulnerability to interconnected global risks; climate change, air and water pollution, ecosystem degradation, and resource pressures compound with economic, infrastructural, health, and institutional weaknesses.
Reducing environmental vulnerability is not exclusively a climate objective—it is simultaneously a public-health, economic-development, infrastructure, and human-development objective.

Integrating climate adaptation, pollution reduction, clean energy transitions, environmental infrastructure, and ecosystem protection cuts global environmental vulnerability from 67.5 (2025) to 10.5 by 2100 (-84.4%), compared with 92.0 under unmitigated drift.

Ex-ante environmental resilience investments deliver 7.3x–10.8x social benefit-cost ratios, outperforming reactive post-disaster cleanups (1.5x) while simultaneously lowering chronic morbidity and stabilizing food and water systems.
